brand.tagline: Define the finished house. Not the way to build it.
brand.rule: You own WHAT and WHY. Your contractor owns HOW.

buckets.name: Demo & Dumpster
buckets.hint: State what must be gone and what condition the space is left in. Not how it comes out.
lines: All flooring removed down to bare subfloor; subfloor left clean, dry, and sound
All existing kitchen cabinets, counters, and appliances removed and hauled off
All bathroom fixtures, vanities, and tile removed to bare stud and subfloor
Interior walls scheduled for removal are gone and the openings are framed ready
All ceiling material removed; ceiling joists left exposed and clean
All interior doors, trim, and casing removed
All debris hauled off site; no debris stored on the lot overnight
Site left broom clean and walkable at the end of every work day
Existing HVAC equipment, ductwork, and line sets removed
Exterior siding removed to sheathing where noted; sheathing left dry and sound
All abandoned wiring, plumbing, and gas lines removed back to source
Dumpster on site for the full duration; contractor pulls and swaps as needed

buckets.name: Exterior
buckets.hint: State the finished material, the coverage, and the warranty. Not the install method.
lines: Roof is new, watertight, and delivered with a manufacturer warranty in writing
Roof decking replaced anywhere it is soft, rotted, or delaminated
New drip edge, valley flashing, and pipe boots throughout
All siding is uniform in profile and color across every elevation, no patchwork
All exterior wood is primed and painted with no bare wood left anywhere
All windows operate, lock, and are sealed weathertight
Exterior doors are new, weatherstripped, keyed alike, and locking
Gutters and downspouts installed and discharging a minimum of 5 feet from the foundation
Grade slopes away from the foundation on all four sides
Porch and deck framing, decking, and rails are structurally sound and code compliant
Driveway and walkways are safe, level, and free of trip hazards
Yard is cleared, graded, and left with established ground cover
Exterior lighting works at every entry door
Address numbers installed and visible from the street
Crawlspace or basement is dry, sealed, and access is secured
All exterior penetrations are sealed, flashed, and rodent proof

buckets.name: MEPs — Mechanical / Electrical / Plumbing
buckets.hint: State the required pass: inspected and approved to final. Not the routing or the conduit type.
lines: Electrical service and panel are adequate for the finished house and pass inspection
All electrical work is permitted, inspected, and approved to final by the AHJ
Every room has code compliant receptacle spacing, switching, and lighting
GFCI and AFCI protection is in place everywhere code requires it
Smoke and CO detectors installed and interconnected per code
All knob and tube, aluminum, or damaged wiring is removed and replaced
Plumbing supply lines are new throughout and pass pressure test
Drain, waste, and vent system is code compliant and passes inspection
Water heater is new, correctly sized, and permitted
Every fixture drains, holds pressure, and has no leaks at final walk
Main sewer line is camera inspected and the footage is delivered to Owner
HVAC system is sized by load calculation, not by rule of thumb, and the calculation is delivered
HVAC heats and cools every room to within 2 degrees of the thermostat setpoint
All ductwork is sealed, insulated, and delivers measured airflow to every register
Bath and kitchen exhaust vents terminate outside the building, never in an attic or crawl
Gas piping is pressure tested and permitted where gas is present
All MEP rough-in passes inspection before any insulation or drywall goes up
All permits are closed out and copies delivered to Owner

buckets.name: Framing & Drywall
buckets.hint: State the finish level and the result — level, square, ready for paint. Not the fastener schedule.
lines: All structural repairs are engineered where required and the stamped plan is delivered
Floor system is level, solid, and free of bounce and squeaks
All rot, termite, and water damaged framing is removed and replaced
Walls are plumb, square, and true; no visible bows or waves after finish
All new openings are headed and supported per code
Subfloor is flat and sound with no soft spots or deflection
Insulation meets or exceeds code R value in walls, ceiling, and floor
All exterior wall and ceiling penetrations are air sealed before insulation
Drywall is hung, taped, and finished to a smooth Level 4 finish ready for paint
Ceilings are finished flat and consistent throughout, no texture mismatch
All corners are straight and true with no visible tape lines or seams
Existing plaster or drywall that stays is repaired to match the new finish
Attic access is provided, insulated, and weatherstripped
All framing passes inspection before close-in

buckets.name: Kitchen
buckets.hint: Set cabinets, counters, appliances, and finishes by allowance — not by brand, unless the brand drives your ARV.
lines: Kitchen layout is functional with code compliant clearances at every appliance and walkway
New cabinets installed level, plumb, secured to framing, with all doors and drawers adjusted
Counters are templated, fabricated, and installed with finished edges and sealed seams
Sink and faucet are installed, sealed, and leak free
Garbage disposal installed and working with switch in a code compliant location
Dishwasher installed, plumbed, and with a high loop or air gap per code
Range or cooktop installed with vented hood terminating outside
Refrigerator space is correctly sized with water line installed and shutoff accessible
Microwave installed and secured per manufacturer instructions
Backsplash installed, grouted, and sealed
All countertop appliance outlets are GFCI protected and code compliant in spacing
Under cabinet or task lighting installed and switched
Flooring runs continuous under the appliances with no visible gaps or transitions
All cabinet hardware installed, aligned, and tight
All appliances are new, matching finish, and delivered with warranty paperwork

buckets.name: Baths
buckets.hint: State the finished result and the waterproofing standard. The method behind the tile is his problem.
lines: Every bath is fully functional with hot water, working drains, and no leaks
Shower and tub areas are waterproofed and pass a water test before tile
Tile is installed level, with consistent grout lines, and fully sealed
Vanity installed level and secured with sealed countertop and backsplash
Toilet set on a new flange with a new wax ring and secured, no rock
Exhaust fan installed in every bath and vented to the exterior
All bath outlets are GFCI protected
Mirrors, lighting, and accessories installed at consistent heights throughout
Shower door or enclosure installed square, sealed, and operating smoothly
Floor is level with no soft spots and slopes correctly to the shower drain
All valves and trim match in finish across the whole bathroom
Access panel provided at every tub and shower valve
New bath added is permitted, inspected, and closed out

buckets.name: Flooring & Paint
buckets.hint: State coverage, uniformity, and transitions. Sheen and color you can name — technique you cannot.
lines: Flooring is continuous and uniform throughout the main living areas with no color breaks
Subfloor is prepped flat and clean before any flooring is installed
All transitions between rooms and materials are finished with matching trim
Flooring runs into closets and under all appliances
No squeaks, gaps, hollow spots, or lifted edges at final walk
All interior walls, ceilings, and trim are primed and painted to full uniform coverage
No flashing, roller marks, holidays, or lap lines visible in normal daylight
All nail holes, dents, and seams are filled and sanded before paint
Trim and door paint lines are cut sharp with no bleed onto walls
All interior doors are hung, latched, and swing without rubbing or sticking
Baseboard, casing, and shoe mold installed continuous with tight mitered joints
Closet shelving and rods installed and secure
Paint colors and sheens are recorded and one touch-up kit is left on site
All hardware, plates, and covers installed and aligned

buckets.name: Punch + Contingency
buckets.hint: State the walk-through standard and the rule for using contingency. Do not list defects you have not seen yet.
lines: House is professionally cleaned inside and out, move-in ready
All windows and glass are cleaned and free of labels, paint, and overspray
Every door, drawer, window, switch, outlet, and fixture is tested and works at final walk
Owner walk-through happens before final payment and the punch list is written and signed
All punch items are completed within 10 days of the walk-through
All warranties, manuals, and closeout documents are delivered to Owner
All permits are finaled and copies delivered to Owner
Lien releases from the contractor and every sub are delivered before final payment
All keys, remotes, openers, and access codes are delivered to Owner
Contingency is Owner controlled and released only by signed change order
Contingency is for unknown conditions found during the work, not for scope the contractor forgot to bid
Any leftover material purchased with project funds stays with the property

responsibility.hint: Every unmarked row is unfunded work. Mark all twelve.
items: Pull the building permit and pay the permit fees
Hire and pay the engineer if engineering is required
Order and pay for utility work, meters, and disconnects
Take delivery of and store materials on site
Dumpster, portable toilet, and temporary power
Site security, lockbox, and locking the house each night
Schedule all inspections and meet the inspector
Order and pay for termite, sewer scope, or specialty inspections
Snow, weather, and storm protection of open work
Final cleaning before listing or move-in

allowances.hint: An allowance is only real if it has all five: a dollar amount, exactly what it covers including tax and freight and labor, a selection deadline, an overage rule, and an underage rule. Missing one makes it a blank check.

exclusions.hint: Write your exclusions first. Whatever you leave silent, his fine print decides.
lines: Anything not written in this scope of work is not included
No verbal additions, promises, or side agreements are part of this scope
Contractor's own exclusions are not binding unless the Owner initials them
Asbestos, lead, and mold abatement are excluded unless separately scoped and priced
Structural work beyond what is shown requires engineering and a signed change order
Septic and well work is excluded unless separately scoped and priced
Utility upgrades or new service beyond the existing service are excluded
Off-site improvements, sidewalks, and right-of-way work are excluded
Permit and impact fees are not part of the contract price
Any material substitution requires written Owner approval before ordering
Landscaping beyond grading and ground cover is excluded
Appliances not listed here are excluded

gates.hint: Never fund a gate that has not been inspected. Tick the gates you will hold money at and set the percentage.

items.label: Pre-construction — permit in hand, engineering stamped, insurance current
Foundation and structural complete — before backfill, before any interior close-in
Rough-in — MEP inspected and passed before insulation
Close-in — insulation and drywall complete before finishes
Substantial completion — Owner walk with written punch list
Final — all inspections signed off, warranties delivered, lien releases in

rules.hint: The rules that stop most of the bleeding. Tick the ones going in your scope.
lines: Every change order is written and signed by both parties before the work starts. Nothing verbal.
Change order markup is set here, up front, as a fixed percentage of cost
Every change order states its schedule impact in days
Allowance overage requires a signed change order before material is ordered
Bids come back as one number per bucket. No ranges.
Every bidder attaches license, GL and workers comp certificates, and three references
Deposit is capped and tied to a gate, not paid as a lump sum up front
Retainage is held until final and released only at G6

selfcheck: Priced in ranges? Pick one number. A range is his to interpret and your lender's to refuse.
Named a product instead of a result? If you specified it, you own the red tag.
Used the word allowance without all five elements? That is a blank check.
Wrote sequencing as a recommendation, or buried it after the price? Make it contractual.
Left a responsibility row unmarked? Unassigned work is unfunded work.
Skipped your own exclusions? His fine print wins by default.
Wrong altitude — too detailed where you have no authority, too vague where you have all of it?
